board.pickLabel: Select the board you will use:
board.customIntro: The board selector defines how the programmer talks to the FTDI: USB VID/PID and which ADBUS pin carries each signal. FPGA pins are not set here.
board.pcfInProject: FPGA pins (LED, BTN, CLK, TX…) live in {name}, one more project file: you edit it, rename it, and it is exported with the rest.
board.storageNotice: This data is stored in this browser on this computer (local storage). If you switch computers or browsers, it will not be there.
board.name: Name
board.fpgaPartHint: Device and package of the iCE40 on your board. They decide which pins are valid in the .pcf.
board.usbHint: VID and PID of the FTDI chip. Accepts 0x0403 or 1027. Default is the FT2232H (0x0403 / 0x6010).
board.usbBad: VID and PID must be 16-bit numbers (0x0000 to 0xFFFF).
board.adbusHint: Pick which ADBUS0–7 pin carries each signal. Default is iceprog / Azukar
board.adbusDup: Two signals cannot share the same ADBUS pin.
board.pcfCopied: Added the {board} PCF to the project as {name}.
board.keptFiles: Switched to {name} but kept your files (they were not the previous board’s starter).
board.azukarBlurb: iCE40-HX8K, 8 LEDs, 8 active-low buttons, CLK12 at 12 MHz, UART on TX/RX. Programmer is FT2232H channel A, same iceprog map as Alhambra.
board.eduCiaaBlurb: iCE40-HX4K (nextpnr hx8k / tq144:4k). 4 LEDs, 4 active-low buttons (BTN1 = pin 31). CLK 12 MHz on pin 94. UART TX pin 56, RX pin 55. ADBUS same as Azukar.
board.alhambraBlurb: iCE40-HX4K (nextpnr hx8k / tq144:4k). 8 LEDs (pins 45–37), SW1/SW2 on 34/33 active-low, CLK 12 MHz on pin 49, UART TX 61 / RX 62. Same iceprog ADBUS as Azukar.
board.customBlurb: Profile you built: VID/PID and ADBUS map for programming, device/package for nextpnr. FPGA pins come from the project .pcf.
board.genericBlurb: Listed profile under boards/<id>/. ADBUS goes to the WebUSB programmer; FPGA pins come from the project .pcf.

app.title: Lattice iCE40 FPGA Web Flasher
app.firefoxBody: You can still use the lab: edit Verilog, compile, and download the .bin. The programmer (channel A) needs WebUSB, which Firefox does not support. To flash the board, use Chrome or Edge.
app.firefoxSerial: WebSerial for serial communication UART (channel B) is not native either, but an add-on can enable it:

fpga.closeTab: Close tab (the file stays in the tree)
fpga.noOpenTab: No open tab. Click a file in the tree on the left.
fpga.baudHint: Fixed 8N1. Same baud as the Verilog.
fpga.connectProgrammerHint: Opens FTDI channel A over WebUSB (the programmer). Not the UART.
fpga.disconnectProgrammerHint: Releases channel A. UART (channel B) is untouched.
fpga.reconnectHint: Resets the USB pipe and reconnects without reinstalling the driver.
fpga.downloadBinHint: icepack bitstream (Yosys/nextpnr), not the EEPROM or a flash dump
fpga.sramHint: iceprog -S: into CRAM, not flash. Volatile: Reset reloads the NOR. On this board CS is the same net as the flash CS.
fpga.sramCdoneLow: SRAM: CDONE=0. Slave did not take the bitstream. The log has CS/CRESET/CDONE; To reload from flash, reset the board.
fpga.sramRetryMpsse: SRAM: the fast path did not configure. Retrying over MPSSE GPIO, slower.
fpga.readEepromHint: Reads the small FTDI EEPROM (name/vendor/serial), not the SPI flash
fpga.connectUartHint: WebSerial channel B. Pick Converter B’s COM port, not the programmer.
fpga.disconnectUartHint: Releases the COM port. Programmer (channel A) is untouched.
fpga.logEmpty: Synthesis and programming log (channel A / WebUSB).
fpga.needWebUsb: WebUSB runs in Chrome or Edge, on localhost or HTTPS.
fpga.needWebSerial: WebSerial runs in Chrome or Edge, on localhost or HTTPS.
fpga.needWebSerialFirefox: Firefox has no native WebSerial. An add-on can enable it:
fpga.noUsbDevice: You closed the picker. No board is connected.
fpga.usbClaim: Chrome could not claim the USB interface. Close iceprog and other USB tools; on Windows, Zadig → Converter A → WinUSB.
fpga.usbWinusb: The board showed up, but USB is not talking. On Windows: Zadig → USB Serial Converter A (Interface 0) → WinUSB.
fpga.usbShortRead: Flash read failed (short USB packet). On Windows 10 this can happen with certain USB host controllers. Unplug, wait a few seconds, and plug in again. Try a different USB port if it persists.
fpga.usbDenied: The browser blocked USB. Use localhost or HTTPS, and accept the picker.
fpga.usbTimeout: The flash did not respond in time. Check the cable, power, and the WinUSB driver.
fpga.usbEmptyBin: That .bin is empty or erased flash (all 0xFF).
fpga.usbJedec: Could not recognize the flash chip (JEDEC).
fpga.usbUnknown: Could not talk to the board. Details are in the programmer log.
fpga.zipNoVerilog: The zip has no .v files (name like and2.v).
fpga.zipNoFiles: The zip has no valid files with allowed extensions ({exts}).
fpga.zipImported: Imported {n} file(s) from {name}. Not saved; lives in this window.
fpga.compileQueuedBrowser: In this browser (YoWASP): Yosys → nextpnr-ice40 → icepack…
fpga.compileBadInput: The top name, a .v file, or the PCF is not valid.
fpga.compileNoPcf: This project has no .pcf. nextpnr needs one to know which pin each signal goes to.
fpga.compileManyPcf: There is more than one .pcf in the project. Keep a single one to compile.
fpga.pcfNoneBody: nextpnr needs a constraint file to know which FPGA pin each signal goes to. This is the one for the active board: add it as {name} and edit it as you like.
fpga.pcfNoneNoBoard: This board ships no example PCF. Create a .pcf file in the project with your set_io lines.
fpga.pcfManyBody: I will not guess which one to compile. Keep a single one in the project and try again. I found:
fpga.resetProjectBody: You will lose every file in this project, the .pcf included, and the {name} lab comes back. This cannot be undone: export the zip first if you want to keep them.
fpga.projectResetDone: Project reset to the board lab.
fpga.projectRestored: Project restored from the browser ({n} files).
fpga.projectTooBig: The project is too big to store in the browser: it will not come back on reload. Export the zip.
fpga.compileWorker: Could not load Yosys/nextpnr in the browser.
fpga.uartNoReadable: That COM port is not readable. Pick Converter B (UART), not the programmer.
fpga.eraseConfirm: This erases the whole flash. The design is gone until you program again. Sure?
fpga.flashEmpty: Flash empty (all 0xFF). Not downloading a .bin: nothing to re-program.
fpga.flashBinSaved: Downloaded azukar-flash.bin ({n} B){note}. That is the one you re-upload.
fpga.uploadEmpty: Loaded {name} but it is empty or erased flash (all 0xFF).
fpga.noBinTitle: No .bin. Compile from the editor or upload one?
fpga.connectPicker: [mpsse] Connect: pick the board in the picker (I do not reuse the last one)
fpga.compileHint: Synthesizes the project for the selected board (Yosys → nextpnr → icepack).
fpga.exportConsoleHint: Downloads the whole log as consola.txt, to read it comfortably or send it.
fpga.resetHint: Reloads the FPGA from flash, like a board reset.

ide.autoCheckHint: Runs the quick check when you stop typing. It starts after the first compile or check, once the WASM is in the browser.
ide.checkHint: Reads the .v files and runs hierarchy -check: syntax errors and missing modules in seconds, no place & route (Ctrl+S).
ide.cancelHint: Stops the running compile. WASM cannot abort, so the worker is restarted.
ide.noProblems: No problems. Compile or check to see them here.
ide.noReport: Nothing compiled yet: chip usage and Fmax show up here.
ide.verifyOk: Verify OK: the flash matches the .bin.
ide.noConstraintHint: That clock has no set_frequency in the .pcf, so nextpnr compares it against its 12 MHz default. Add `set_frequency CLK 12` (or the real frequency) to make the result mean something.

tools.menuHint: Share, disk folder, PLL, ROM and hex viewer
tools.artifactMissing: I do not have {name}: compile once and try again.

offline.cleared: Offline cache cleared: the next load downloads the WASM again.

share.title: Share the project as a link
share.intro: The {n} files travel compressed inside the link, after the #. Whoever opens it gets the project exactly as it is here.
share.tooLong: The link is long: some browsers and mail clients may cut it. Drop files or use the zip instead.
share.privacy: Text after the # never reaches the server: it stays in both browsers.
share.badLink: That shared link could not be read.
share.openBody: The link carries a project with {n} file(s). Opening it replaces what you have in the editor.

pll.title: PLL wizard
pll.intro: Runs icepll (the IceStorm one, in WebAssembly) and writes the module with the dividers already worked out.
pll.usePad: SB_PLL40_PAD (clock comes in through a PAD pin)
pll.off: ({n} MHz away from what you asked)
pll.badInput: Input clock must be between 10 and 133 MHz.
pll.badOutput: Output clock must be between 16 and 275 MHz.
pll.badName: Module name must be a Verilog identifier.
pll.failed: icepll could not hit that combination.

icebram.title: Swap the contents of a ROM
icebram.intro: icebram replaces BRAM data inside the bitstream that is already compiled. Change the table and the .bin comes out in seconds, no re-synthesis.
icebram.needCompile: Compile once first: icebram works on the .asc from that compile.
icebram.noHex: No .hex files in the project. Generate one below or add it with the + button.
icebram.genIntro: icebram -g writes random values. Use it as the initial contents: the design reads it with $readmemh and you swap it later.
icebram.done: ROM swapped: new bitstream of {n} bytes.
icebram.failed: icebram could not swap the ROM. Usually two reasons: the current .hex is not the one that was compiled, or its data repeats and it cannot locate it in the bitstream ("Conflicting from pattern" in the log). Generate the initial contents with the Generate button, which writes random values.
icebram.badName: The file name must be valid and end in .hex.
icebram.HEX_BAD_CHAR: it has characters that are not hex digits
icebram.HEX_RAGGED: the words do not all have the same width
icebram.HEX_NOT_256: the number of words must be a multiple of 256
icebram.HEX_WIDTH: both .hex files must have the same word width
icebram.HEX_DEPTH: both .hex files must have the same number of words

uart.plotHint: Plots lines that are only numbers (12, 34 or temp:21.5), like the Arduino serial plotter.
uart.logSaved: Saved the UART log as uart.txt.
uart.endingHint: What gets appended to what you send
uart.writeFailed: This port does not accept writes.

folder.noPermission: The browser did not grant write permission on the folder.
folder.closed: Released folder {name}: “Save to folder” will ask again.
folder.renamed: Renamed on import (spaces do not survive the toolchain): {list}.

project.label: Project
project.selectHint: Projects live in this browser. Switching saves the current one.
project.new: New project, with the active board's lab
project.removeBody: This removes “{name}” from this browser, with all its files. It cannot be undone: export the zip first if you want to keep it.
